methods.label: Find and verify a repeating block
methods.explanation:
Compute several terms to see what the digit rule does. Let \(t_n\) denote the \(n\)th term, with \(t_1=2005\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
t_2&=2^3+0^3+0^3+5^3=133,\\
t_3&=1^3+3^3+3^3=55,\\
t_4&=5^3+5^3=250,\\
t_5&=2^3+5^3+0^3=133.
\end{aligned}
\]
The value \(133\) has returned. Because the next term depends only on the digits of the current term, the same three transitions must now repeat forever. Starting at term \(2\), the repeating block is therefore \(133,55,250\).

There are
\[
2005-2+1=2004=3\cdot668
\]
terms from term \(2\) through term \(2005\), inclusive. These form \(668\) complete blocks, so the last term is the third entry of a block: \(\boxed{250}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
